title: India's Young Shuttlers Take Centre Stage at Malaysia Masters as Sindhu and Satwik-Chirag Sit Out
excerpt: Lakshya Sen leads a 26-member squad to Kuala Lumpur in what could be a defining week for Indian badminton's next generation and 2028 Olympic qualification
body:
## Young Guard, New Horizons

When the draw for the 2026 Malaysia Masters was finalised last week, the absences were conspicuous. PV Sindhu — the two-time winner whose name is virtually synonymous with Indian badminton on the global stage — had withdrawn. So had Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, the men's doubles pair who reached the Thailand Open final just days earlier. In a sport where India's overseas ambitions are measured almost entirely through the fortunes of its biggest names, the holes in the squad might have suggested a country in retreat.

The opposite is true. India's 26-member contingent for the BWF Super 500 tournament at Axiata Arena in Kuala Lumpur, which begins on Tuesday, is younger, deeper, and arguably more consequential for the future of Indian badminton than any single headline performance by its established stars could be.

## Lakshya Sen Leads the Charge

At the vanguard is **Lakshya Sen**, seeded eighth, who enters Malaysia as India's undisputed men's singles spearhead. The 24-year-old from Almora has had a turbulent 18 months — a fourth-place heartbreak at the Paris Olympics, a back injury that sidelined him for months, and a string of early exits that briefly pushed him outside the world's top 20. But a gutsy run at the Australian Open earlier this year and improved form at the Thailand Open suggest that the Sen who once stunned the All England crowd in 2022 is slowly finding his way back.

He will be joined by **HS Prannoy**, the 2023 Malaysia Masters champion, whose dogged defensive game and experience at the venue make him India's most dangerous floater. **Kiran George** and **Tharun Mannepalli** round out the men's singles squad, both under 23 and part of the Bangalore-based pipeline at the Prakash Padukone academy that has produced India's last three world-ranked shuttlers.

## The Women's Draw: Hooda and the Next Wave

In the women's singles, the story is youth. **Unnati Hooda**, seeded sixth at just 18, is the highest-ranked Indian in the draw and one of the youngest players to carry that distinction in a Super 500 event this season. Behind her, **Malvika Bansod** and **Anmol Kharb** — both products of the SAI-backed training centres that have expanded dramatically since 2021 — represent a generation that has grown up watching Sindhu and Saina Nehwal on television and entered the sport with none of the infrastructure deficits their predecessors faced.

**Aakarshi Kashyap** returns to BWF World Tour competition for the first time since the Orleans Masters in March, starting from the qualifiers. Her comeback, after a knee injury that threatened to derail her career, will be watched closely by selectors eyeing the 2026 Asian Games squad.

## The Doubles Puzzle

India's doubles representation is thinner. In the absence of Satwik-Chirag, the men's doubles challenge falls to **MR Arjun and Hariharan Amsakarunan**, a pair still building their international profile. In women's doubles, **Rutaparna and Swetaparna Panda** — the sister duo from Odisha — and **Ashwini Bhat K/Shikha Gautam** carry the flag, while mixed doubles features three emerging combinations: Ashith Surya/Amrutha Pramuthesh, Rohan Kapoor/Ruthvika Shivani Gadde, and Sathwik Reddy Kanapuram/Radhika Sharma.

None of these pairings is ranked inside the world's top 30. That is precisely the point. Major absences create opportunity, and the Badminton Association of India's willingness to send a 26-strong squad — significantly larger than most nations — reflects a deliberate strategy to blood younger players at the highest available level.

## Where to Watch from Abroad

For the estimated **3.2 million NRIs** who follow Indian badminton — the sport consistently ranks among the top three most-watched Olympic disciplines in the diaspora — the Malaysia Masters will be streamed live in India. Depending on regional broadcasting agreements, Viacom18's JioCinema and Star Sports typically carry BWF Super 500 events. Diaspora viewers in the US, UK, and Canada can access BWF TV's pay-per-event stream or check their local sports broadcasters for coverage details.

## What's at Stake

The Malaysia Masters is more than a mid-tier tournament for India's contingent. Every ranking point earned here feeds directly into the Olympic qualification cycle for the 2028 Los Angeles Games, where India is expected to field its largest-ever badminton team. For Sen, a deep run would cement his return to the world's top 10. For Hooda, it could announce her arrival as India's next marquee women's singles player. And for the doubles pairs, even a round or two of victories would justify the BAI's investment in a broader bench.

Indian badminton's golden era was built by individual brilliance. Its next chapter, if the Malaysia Masters contingent is any guide, will be built by depth.
